b: Anand George is the celebrated chef and founder of Cardiff’s iconic Purple Poppadom , widely credited with re-imagining Indian dining in the UK. Originally from Kerala, he trained at the Taj Group’s prestigious hotel…
f: Anand George is the celebrated chef and founder of Cardiff’s iconic Purple Poppadom , widely credited with re-imagining Indian dining in the UK. Originally from Kerala, he trained at the Taj Group’s prestigious hotel management school in Aurangabad, graduating with a gold medal in Culinary Arts and Kitchen Administration, before honing his skills at leading luxury hotels including The Oberoi Vanyavilas, Taj Coromandel, and The Leela. Rooted in Kerala’s rich food heritage and driven by innovation, he went on to launch the trend-setting Indian street-food venture Tukka Tuk , now operating in Cardiff, Swansea, and Barry. Purple Poppadom has earned Michelin Guide recognition, Good Food Guide listings, acclaim from critics such as Jay Rayner, and major honours including Best South Asian Restaurant in the UK and Best Restaurant in Wales at the British Curry Awards. Beyond the restaurant, he shares his culinary journey through his bestselling memoir-cookbook The 5,000-Mile Journey , tracing his path from Cochin to Cardiff. He was invited as a speaker to the Jaipur Literature Festival in London (2024) and Jaipur (2025). For Anand, food is a multi-sensory experience—“we eat with our eyes, nose, and tongue”—and his work continues to celebrate innovation rooted in authenticity.
s: Is Food Becoming Fast, Just to Make a Fast Billion?

She currently serves as Associate Professor, Research Guide, and Head of the Department of English at The Zamorin’s Guruvayurappan College, University of Calicut, Kerala. b: Ayesha Gamiet is an artist, illustrator and educator. Rooted in the rich visual language of Islamic art and the natural world, her work reinterprets traditional forms, motifs, and narratives for a contemporary context.…
f: Ayesha Gamiet is an artist, illustrator and educator. Rooted in the rich visual language of Islamic art and the natural world, her work reinterprets traditional forms, motifs, and narratives for a contemporary context. Drawing inspiration from Persian and Indian miniature painting, illuminated manuscripts, poetry, and storytelling, her practice reflects a range of cultural influences. Employing traditional methods and techniques, she creates paintings that are part representational and part fantastical, celebrating the beauty of the natural world and evoking the magic of the everyday. She trained at the King’s Foundation School of Traditional Arts, specialising in Islamic manuscript illumination and miniature painting. In 2018, she completed an apprenticeship in manuscript illumination under Master Illuminators Ayten Tiryaki and Çiçek Derman in Istanbul. She was subsequently commissioned by the Royal Library at Windsor Castle to illuminate frontispieces for four volumes of poetry gifted to HM Queen Elizabeth II, HM The King, and poet Imtiaz Dharker. The final volume was acquired by the Royal Collection Trust. An award-winning illustrator and trained teacher, she holds a PGCE in Art and Design and an MEd in Art, Creativity and Culture in Education from the University of Cambridge. She has provided training for new art teachers at the Cambridge University Faculty of Education and delivered public workshops at the Queen’s Gallery, Buckingham Palace. She has also taught extensively on the King’s Foundation School for Traditional Arts public and international programmes.

f: Bony Thomas is a short story writer and illustrator based in Kadavanthra, Kochi. He is the author of Kochiites ( കൊച്ചിക്കാർ ), a study of cultural pluralism in the Fort Kochi–Mattancherry region, and Dogspace , a collection of short stories. He directs Walk with Bony , a social media series of micro-documentaries exploring the cultural history of Fort Kochi and Mattancherry, and has undertaken the Kochi Cultural Heritage Mapping project for the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA). One of the founders of the Kochi Biennale Foundation, which organises the Kochi–Muziris Biennale, India’s international contemporary art festival, he is also a recipient of the UNESCO–Sahapedia Fellowship for his study on boat builders in Kochi. Previously, he worked as a senior cartoonist and illustrator with The Economic Times in Mumbai and Delhi, and is currently the Nodal Officer at the Cochin Heritage Zone Conservation Society.

f: Bose Krishnamachari is an artist, independent curator, scenographer and cultural activist. He is the co-founder and ideator of the Kochi Biennale Foundation and the Kochi-Muziris Biennale, one of the most significant contemporary art events in Asia. A graduate of Sir J.J.School of Art and taught in 1992, later with a Master’s in Fine Art from Goldsmiths, University of London, his interdisciplinary practice spans painting, installation, design, and institution building. He has curated major national and international exhibitions, including the inaugural Kochi-Muziris Biennale (2012), the Indian Pavilion at ARCO Madrid (2009), and the Yinchuan Biennale (MoCA),China (2016). He has been the Artistic Director of Gallery DTALE ARCHIST and founder of Gallery BMB. His ongoing educational empowerment–travel initiative, LaVA (Laboratory of Visual Art), reflects his commitment to pedagogy, and he was among the designers who showcased their work at the second edition of the ADFF:STIR Pavilion Park. His accolades include the Asia Society’s Game Changer Award, the Charles Wallace Award, and Kerala Lalithakala Akademi’s ‘Lifetime Fellowship’. Listed in Art Review’s Power100 and GQ Men of the Year 2025, he lives and works between Mumbai and Kochi.
s: The Afterlife of an Art: What Happens to Art Once Their Contemporary World Dissolves

He served as an IAS officer in Manipur and Kerala from 1977-1983. He then resigned to become an entrepreneur. In 1985, Balagopal set up a startup using knowhow developed at a National Lab, and grew it over the next 20 years into the world`s largest producer of blood bag systems. He has also authored several books, including On a Clear Day You Can See India , The View from Kollam , Maveli & Markets , and his latest work, Below the Radar. Balagopal and his wife Vinita run the Anaha Trust that supports social enterprises in Kerala and Manipur.

bk.t: On a clear day you can see India

b: C K Janu is a tribal rights activist from the Adiya community in Mananthavady, Wayanad district. She is the leader of Adivasi Gothra Maha Sabha, a social movement that has been agitating since 2001 for redistribution of…
f: C K Janu is a tribal rights activist from the Adiya community in Mananthavady, Wayanad district. She is the leader of Adivasi Gothra Maha Sabha, a social movement that has been agitating since 2001 for redistribution of land to the landless tribal people in Kerala with their resounding slogan, ‘Right to live in the land one is born.’ Janu was the face of the Muthanga agitation by adivasis to demand the land promised to them by the Kerala government. Her autobiography Mother Forest: The Unfinished Story of C K Janu was published in 2004.

b: C K Vineeth is a professional football player who plays as a forward or right midfielder and is currently with Thrissur Magic FC in the Super League Kerala. He is best known for his successful stints with Bengaluru FC…
f: C K Vineeth is a professional football player who plays as a forward or right midfielder and is currently with Thrissur Magic FC in the Super League Kerala. He is best known for his successful stints with Bengaluru FC and Kerala Blasters FC.

b: An esteemed author, feminist and academician, C S Chandrika is a trailblazer in the field of Malayalam literature. A front-line activist of the Kerala Feminist Movement of the 90’s, she is also active as a director,…
f: An esteemed author, feminist and academician, C S Chandrika is a trailblazer in the field of Malayalam literature. A front-line activist of the Kerala Feminist Movement of the 90’s, she is also active as a director, researcher and columnist. Her works have been translated into various languages like English, Kannada and Tamil. Her major works include Pira, Kaanthal, Ladies Compartment , Keralathile Sthree Munnettathinte Charithram, and Kleptomania among others.

b: C V Balakrishnan is a versatile novelist, short-story writer and screenwriter writing in Malayalam. His oeuvre comprises more than sixty works across several genres. His works titled Athmavinu Sheri Enn Thonunna…
f: C V Balakrishnan is a versatile novelist, short-story writer and screenwriter writing in Malayalam. His oeuvre comprises more than sixty works across several genres. His works titled Athmavinu Sheri Enn Thonunna Karyangal , Paralmeen Neenthunna Padam and Ethetho Saraninkalil won the Kerala Sahitya Academy Awards, and his study titled Cinemayude Idangal won the State Award for Best Book on Cinema. He has also won several Awards for Overall Contributions such as the Muttathu Varkey Award, the Padmaprabha Award, the Basheer Award and the O Chandu Menon Award, among other accolades. Ezhuthinte Althaara is his latest collection of short stories.

b: C. S. Venkiteswaran is an Indian film critic, professor, documentary filmmaker, and writer. He is the author of Samanthara Yathrakal – K. R. Mohanante Cinema , a critical study of filmmaker K. R. Mohanan, and co-editor…
f: C. S. Venkiteswaran is an Indian film critic, professor, documentary filmmaker, and writer. He is the author of Samanthara Yathrakal – K. R. Mohanante Cinema , a critical study of filmmaker K. R. Mohanan, and co-editor of A Door to Adoor , a book on Adoor Gopalakrishnan, with Lalit Mohan Joshi. His book Malayala Cinema Padanangal received a Special Jury Mention at the Kerala State Film Awards (2011). He won the National Film Award for Best Arts/Cultural Film (1995), along with M. R. Rajan, for Pakarnattam – Ammannur, The Actor , a lyrical cinematic documentation of the life of Ammannur Madhava Chakyar. He is the recipient of several prestigious honours, including the National Film Award for Best Film Critic (2009) and the National Film Award for Best Arts/Cultural Film (1995).

b: Cameron Noble began his appointment as Deputy Consul General at the Australia Consulate General in Chennai in December 2025. Prior to this he was the Acting Director, Pacific Integration Section, Office of the Pacific…
f: Cameron Noble began his appointment as Deputy Consul General at the Australia Consulate General in Chennai in December 2025. Prior to this he was the Acting Director, Pacific Integration Section, Office of the Pacific in the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) delivering innovative mobility and access programs for Pacific Island States. From 2020 to 2024 he was the Political First Secretary at Australia’s Embassy in Tokyo. He was seconded from DFAT to the Australian Civil Military Centre as DFAT’s Foreign Policy Advisor and worked closely with the Australian Defence Force and Australia Federal Police between 2018 and 2020.He has held a range of positions within DFAT including in the Indonesia Political, Japan, and G20 sections. In parallel, he was a long serving officer in the DFAT Crisis Response Team where responded to regional disasters and crises including as the department lead for the 2018 Thai Cave Rescue.

b: Captain Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair is an Indian Air Force (IAF) pilot and astronaut. A recipient of the prestigious Sword of Honour at the Air Force Academy, Hyderabad, he is among the four astronauts selected for the…
f: Captain Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair is an Indian Air Force (IAF) pilot and astronaut. A recipient of the prestigious Sword of Honour at the Air Force Academy, Hyderabad, he is among the four astronauts selected for the Indian Space Research Organisation’s (ISRO) Gaganyaan mission, India’s first human spaceflight programme. An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, he was commissioned into the IAF fighter stream in December 1998. A highly experienced test pilot and flight instructor, he has logged approximately 3,000 hours of flying, operating a wide range of aircraft. He has served as the Commanding Officer of a Su-30 squadron and graduated top of his class from the US Air Force Air Command and Staff College in Alabama. In 2019, he was selected by ISRO for advanced astronaut training at the Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center in Star City, Moscow, where he trained for one year. On February 27, 2024, Prime Minister Narendra Modi officially announced him as one of the astronauts undergoing training for Gaganyaan, marking a historic milestone in India’s space exploration journey.
s: Developing an Astronaut Mindset towards Nation Building

b: Suresh Pillai is a renowned Michelin-star chef and restaurateur with 14 years of experience working at prestigious London restaurants like Veeraswamy and Gymkhana. He has started his own restaurant chain branded…
f: Suresh Pillai is a renowned Michelin-star chef and restaurateur with 14 years of experience working at prestigious London restaurants like Veeraswamy and Gymkhana. He has started his own restaurant chain branded Restaurant Chef Pillar and another one at hotel Le Meridien, Kochi. He also serves as a guest lecturer and guest chef at University of the Bahamas in its Culinary and Hospitality Management Institute. He has also written a book named Thenga Manga: The Art of Kerala Cuisine published by DC Books.

b: Christo John is an aspiring actor and maker, driven by storytelling and visual expression. He brings ideas to life through performance and cinematic craft, constantly learning and evolving to create work that connects…
f: Christo John is an aspiring actor and maker, driven by storytelling and visual expression. He brings ideas to life through performance and cinematic craft, constantly learning and evolving to create work that connects emotionally. He is inspired by real moments, subtle emotions, and powerful visuals. His focus is on creating honest, immersive stories that stay with the audience even after the frame fades.

b: Christopher Kloeble is an award-winning scriptwriter and the author of five novels , a short story collection and a memoir. He has taught at Dartmouth College , Cambridge University and Hong Kong University , among…
f: Christopher Kloeble is an award-winning scriptwriter and the author of five novels , a short story collection and a memoir. He has taught at Dartmouth College , Cambridge University and Hong Kong University , among others . His books have been translated into ten languages. He lives in Berlin and New Delhi. The English translation of his novel, "The Museum of the World, ' which will be adapted for the stage, was published with HarperCollins India.
s: Cross-Cultural Intersections in Art and Literature

b: Claudia Kaiser is Vice President, Business Development of Frankfurt Book Fair. A trained bookseller, she lived in China for more than ten years, working as an editor for China Foreign Literature Publishing House and…
f: Claudia Kaiser is Vice President, Business Development of Frankfurt Book Fair. A trained bookseller, she lived in China for more than ten years, working as an editor for China Foreign Literature Publishing House and later started an agency. She has been in the senior management of the Frankfurt Book Fair since 2003, General Manager of KITAB (Abu Dhabi International Book Fair) and head of the Cape Town Book Fair, among others. She was the main driver in building the platform StoryDrive Asia in Singapore.
s: What sells? Publishing in Germany and India

b: Cornelia Funke is a world-renowned German author and illustrator. S he is best known for her fantasy novels that blend magic with real-world emotional depth, selling over 22 million copies worldwide. Some of her notable…
f: Cornelia Funke is a world-renowned German author and illustrator. S he is best known for her fantasy novels that blend magic with real-world emotional depth, selling over 22 million copies worldwide. Some of her notable works include The Inkheart Series , MirrorWorld (Reckless) Series , and The Thief Lord , among others. In Tuscany, she established "Fraggina" and "Mulinaccio", artist-in-residence programs that host illustrators, writers, and conservationists from around the world. She is deeply involved in environmental and social causes through her Rim of Heaven Foundation and serves as a patron for several charities, including the Ecologia Youth Trust and the Jane Goodall Institute.
s: It's alive!: How writers build worlds (Online session)

b: D. P. Abhijith is a notable Malayalam author. He has been writing stories and poems in reputed journals. His first short story collection Blood Revolution published by DC Books was widely acclaimed. He is currently a…
f: D. P. Abhijith is a notable Malayalam author. He has been writing stories and poems in reputed journals. His first short story collection Blood Revolution published by DC Books was widely acclaimed. He is currently a researcher in Malayalam at Kerala University.

b: David Wagner was born in 1971, and has lived in Berlin since 1991. His prize-winning debut Meine nachtblaue Hose ( My Night-Blue Trousers ) was published in 2000, and his novel Vier Äpfel ( Four Apples ) was…
f: David Wagner was born in 1971, and has lived in Berlin since 1991. His prize-winning debut Meine nachtblaue Hose ( My Night-Blue Trousers ) was published in 2000, and his novel Vier Äpfel ( Four Apples ) was long-listed for the German Book Prize. His best-selling novel, Leben ( Lives ) about a lifesaving organ transplant won the 2013 Leipzig Book Fair Prize and the Best Foreign Novel of the Year Award 2014 in the People's Republic of China. He was Friedrich Dürrenmatt Guest Professor for World Literature at University Bern and his books have been translated into 17 languages, including Marathi. He has written extensively about the city of Berlin in collections such as Mauer Park (2001) Welche Farbe hat Berlin ( What Colour Is Berlin, 2011) and Verlaufen in Berlin (Getting Lost in Berlin , 2021) . His novel Der vergessliche Riese ( The forgetful giant ) won the Bayerische Literaturpreis 2019. In 2024 he published Verkin , a novel about the life and the adventures of a Turkish Armenian woman from Istanbul.
s: Room for Imagination: Writers in Residence

b: Davinci Suresh is a familiar face for Malayalis through his works. Over the years, he has created portraits of Good Samaritan Noushad with clothes, Prithviraj with wood, Fahadh with 8,500 nails, Mohanlal using utensils…
f: Davinci Suresh is a familiar face for Malayalis through his works. Over the years, he has created portraits of Good Samaritan Noushad with clothes, Prithviraj with wood, Fahadh with 8,500 nails, Mohanlal using utensils and Mammootty with paper collage. He use AI for attractive animated works. The Kodungaloor-based artist, who specialises in moving sculptures, is a movie buff and gets creative when it comes to creating portraits of his favourite actors.

b: Deedi Damodaran is a Malayalam screenwriter and an academician with her expertise in the area of film and female. A founder member of the Women in Cinema Collective (WCC), she is a feminist activist working at the…
f: Deedi Damodaran is a Malayalam screenwriter and an academician with her expertise in the area of film and female. A founder member of the Women in Cinema Collective (WCC), she is a feminist activist working at the intersections of cinema, gender, and labour. Her work spans research, writing, and advocacy for equity, ethics, and women’s rights in the film industry.
s: Kiss of Love : ഒരു സമരത്തിന്റെ വ്യാഴവട്ടം

b: Deepa Anappara is a journalist and author whose debut novel, Djinn Patrol on the Purple Line was shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Indian Literature. Time included it in its list of ‘The 100 Best Mystery and Thriller…
f: Deepa Anappara is a journalist and author whose debut novel, Djinn Patrol on the Purple Line was shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Indian Literature. Time included it in its list of ‘The 100 Best Mystery and Thriller Books of All Time’. Her journalism, which focuses on the impact of poverty and religious violence on children’s education, has earned her the Developing Asia Journalism Awards, the Every Human Has Rights Media Awards, and the Sanskriti-Prabha Dutt Fellowship in Journalism.
s: The Last of Earth: A Novel of Exile, Identity & Tibetan Life

b: Dr. Denise DeCaires Narain is Emeritus Reader in Postcolonial Literatures at the University of Sussex. She taught courses on postcolonial, Caribbean and women’s writing and on postcolonial feminist discourses. She has…
f: Dr. Denise DeCaires Narain is Emeritus Reader in Postcolonial Literatures at the University of Sussex. She taught courses on postcolonial, Caribbean and women’s writing and on postcolonial feminist discourses. She has published widely on Caribbean women’s writing, including two monographs, Contemporary Caribbean Women’s Poetry: Making Style and Writers and Their Work: Olive Senior , as well as several essays from current research on the representation of servants in postcolonial women’s writing. She is co-editor for Palgrave’s Contemporary Women’s Writing series and co-editor of the journal Women: A Cultural Review .

b: Dhanya P. Vasu is an academician with postgraduate degrees in Physics and Education and currently serves as the District Project Coordinator, Samagra Shiksha Kerala, Kottayam. She has played a key role in mainstreaming…
f: Dhanya P. Vasu is an academician with postgraduate degrees in Physics and Education and currently serves as the District Project Coordinator, Samagra Shiksha Kerala, Kottayam. She has played a key role in mainstreaming thousands of out-of-school, tribal, and migrant labour children through focused parental awareness and inclusion initiatives. In 2011, she pioneered the first school-based Special Training Centre for multilingual children at Perumbavoor. She is a recipient of the National Award for Educational Administration (2018–19) conferred by NIEPA, Ministry of Education, Government of India. Her academic work includes over 20 research publications, with a strong focus on marginalised education, particularly tribal communities, migrant labour children, and children with special needs.

b: Dileep Narayanan is a purpose-driven brand strategist and sustainability advocate with over 25 years of expertise in Purpose and Sustainability Communication. He is the founder and Managing Directory of Organic BPS - a…
f: Dileep Narayanan is a purpose-driven brand strategist and sustainability advocate with over 25 years of expertise in Purpose and Sustainability Communication. He is the founder and Managing Directory of Organic BPS - a pioneering brand consultancy organisation. He also leads the Greenstorm Foundation, a creative conservancy dedicated to inspiring environmental awareness among youth. Under his leadership, the Greenstorm Global Photography Festival has engaged over 12 million young minds across 150+ countries, earning international recognition, including the IAA Olive Crown Award. He serves on the Advisory Board of Asset Homes Pvt. Ltd. and has previously held advisory roles with the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). As the Honorary Treasurer (formerly Secretary) of the Kerala Management Association, he actively promotes the philosophy of "Growth for All. Growth for Good."

b: Dilip M. Menon is the Professor of History and International Relations at the University of Witwatersrand, and the Director of the Centre for Indian Studies in Africa. An acclaimed historian of South Asia, Professor…
f: Dilip M. Menon is the Professor of History and International Relations at the University of Witwatersrand, and the Director of the Centre for Indian Studies in Africa. An acclaimed historian of South Asia, Professor Menon was awarded the 2021 Falling Walls Foundation Prize for Social Sciences and Humanities. His publications include Blindness of Insight: Essays on Caste in Modern India and the co-edited volumes Cinemas of the Global South: Towards a Southern Aesthetics ; Ocean as Method: Thinking with the Maritime ; Capitalisms: Towards a Global History .
s: The Intimate and Infinite: The Currents, The Merchants, Maps and Refugees of the Indian Ocean World

b: Divya Dugar is a journalist and storyteller with over fifteen years of experience covering news and producing long-form documentaries. Previously, she worked as a producer on more than sixty reports/documentaries for…
f: Divya Dugar is a journalist and storyteller with over fifteen years of experience covering news and producing long-form documentaries. Previously, she worked as a producer on more than sixty reports/documentaries for European broadcasters, primarily ARTE. She has also been a journalist for four years with France 2. Divya's writing has appeared in numerous publications (including The Book of Dog , edited by Hemali Sodhi and published by HarperCollins) and often draws from her love for animals, heritage architecture, train travel and places just off the beaten path. Chaos in a Coupe: Travelling across India with Three Dogs is her most recent book.
s: Friend or Foe? Our Uneasy Relationship with India's Dogs

b: Dr. Ajmal Mueen is an Indian historian, academic, and heritage consultant based in Kerala. He currently serves as the Professor and Head of the Department of History at Muhammed Abdurahiman Memorial Orphanage College in…
f: Dr. Ajmal Mueen is an Indian historian, academic, and heritage consultant based in Kerala. He currently serves as the Professor and Head of the Department of History at Muhammed Abdurahiman Memorial Orphanage College in Mukkam, Kozhikode. He is the Director of the Calicut Heritage Walk initiative which conducts guided tours through the historic streets of Kozhikode to educate the public about the city's multicultural past, including its Arab and European connections. He frequently collaborates with historical organizations like the Archival and Research Project (ARPO).

b: Dr Arun Zachariah is a veterinarian with extensive field experience in the treatment and management of wild animals. He is presently working as the Forest Veterinary Officer in the Kerala Forest Department. With rich…
f: Dr Arun Zachariah is a veterinarian with extensive field experience in the treatment and management of wild animals. He is presently working as the Forest Veterinary Officer in the Kerala Forest Department. With rich national and international academic experience, he plays a pivotal role in managing human–wildlife conflict in Kerala, particularly in the capture and relocation of conflict animals such as tigers, leopards, and elephants. His dedicated team has also contributed significantly to the study and management of various wildlife diseases, including Kyasanur Forest Disease (Monkey Fever), a major zoonotic disease.

b: Dr Ashok Kumar is a Former Professor at Department of Electrical Engineering, College of Engineering, Trivandrum and Consultant, Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC). He is a policy professional…
f: Dr Ashok Kumar is a Former Professor at Department of Electrical Engineering, College of Engineering, Trivandrum and Consultant, Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC). He is a policy professional and innovation ecosystem builder with extensive experience at the intersection of technology, public policy, sustainability, and industrial development. He has authored more than 40 peer-reviewed journal publications and has participated in numerous international conferences, with research contributions in control systems, electrical system design, and power electronics. He is a Senior Member of IEEE and a member of professional bodies including the Indian Society for Technical Education (ISTE), reflecting sustained engagement with the global engineering and academic community. Beyond academia, he has played a key role in conceptualising and coordinating multi-institutional programmes involving government departments, research organisations, industry partners, and startups. His work has been particularly focused on electric mobility, clean energy transition, advanced manufacturing, and innovation-led development, with an emphasis on translating policy vision into practical implementation and linking research excellence with societal and industrial impact.
s: Small State, Big Ideas: Kerala’s Blueprint for Mission-Driven Innovation

b: Dr. Chandradasan , founder of Lokadharmi Nadakaveedu , is a director, designer, writer, actor, and dramaturg. He has designed and directed over 50 plays, including adaptations and interpretations of Western and Indian…
f: Dr. Chandradasan , founder of Lokadharmi Nadakaveedu , is a director, designer, writer, actor, and dramaturg. He has designed and directed over 50 plays, including adaptations and interpretations of Western and Indian classical texts, Shakespeare, contemporary plays, musicals, improvised and devised productions, poetry and short story performances, comedies, and children’s plays. His work spans multiple languages, including Malayalam, Kannada, Finnish, Hindi, Lithuanian, Tamil, Sanskrit, and English. He has published around 50 articles on performance and cultural studies, authored two children’s plays— Bommanahalliyile Kinnara Yogi and Thathamaram —and edited Myriad Spaces: Indian Theatre and Beyond . His latest book, Ramgavatharanathinte Rasasastram , is a collection of articles in Malayalam. An academic and guest faculty at various universities and institutes, he is the recipient of several prestigious literary honours, including the Kerala Sahitya Sangeetha Nataka Academy Award and the Best Playwright Award from the Kerala Bala Sahitya Institute, among others.

b: Dr. K. M. Shareef is an assistant professor at Farook Training College, Kozhikode. He is also a member of several associations including, the Text Book Committee for HSS, the State Resource Group-SCERT, and several…
f: Dr. K. M. Shareef is an assistant professor at Farook Training College, Kozhikode. He is also a member of several associations including, the Text Book Committee for HSS, the State Resource Group-SCERT, and several others. He has published more than thirty articles in various magazines and newspapers and also maintains an active presence in social media.

b: Dr Latha Nair is a distinguished academic leader of international standing, a public intellectual, and an institution builder. A Professor of English Literature and Linguistics, her work spans literary scholarship,…
f: Dr Latha Nair is a distinguished academic leader of international standing, a public intellectual, and an institution builder. A Professor of English Literature and Linguistics, her work spans literary scholarship, gender justice, and the transformation of higher education. She pioneered the establishment of Radio Kochi 90 FM, the first community radio station in the Ernakulam district. She has supported and collaborated with civil society organisations such as Dhisha, Fourth Wave Foundation (Project Venda), and Tata Trust Pilgrims Society. Following her retirement from St. Teresa’s College, she continues to contribute in academic and advisory capacities at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Kochi; Bharathiar University, Coimbatore; Jain University, Kochi; and the DCSMAT Group of Institutions. She is the recipient of a number of prestigious awards and accolades including the Saahas Prerna Award, presented by WISCOMP (Women in Security, Conflict Management and Peace), an initiative of the Foundation for Universal Responsibility, New Delhi. She served as Director of the Gunn Centre in India after completing professional training at Kansas State University, USA and has participated in deliberations at the United Nations General Assembly, contributing to discussions aligned with education, gender, and social justice.
s: Poetry, Power, and the Female Voice
Goddess in Revolt: The Divine Feminine
Why I Killed My Husband & Other Such Stories

b: Dr M C Abdul Nazar is an associate professor of Malayalam department at Sri Sankaracharya Sanskrit University, Kalady. He has worked as a teacher in several government colleges. Vakkinte Sancharangal, Pranayavum…
f: Dr M C Abdul Nazar is an associate professor of Malayalam department at Sri Sankaracharya Sanskrit University, Kalady. He has worked as a teacher in several government colleges. Vakkinte Sancharangal, Pranayavum Swantantriyavum, Urub: Jeevithavum Swatantryavum , Narrations and Representations of Kerala are his published works.

b: Dr. Malavika Binny is a distinguished historian, academic, and writer who currently serves as the Assistant Professor and Head of the Department of History at Kannur University. Her diverse research interests range from…
f: Dr. Malavika Binny is a distinguished historian, academic, and writer who currently serves as the Assistant Professor and Head of the Department of History at Kannur University. Her diverse research interests range from archival studies in Kerala and Europe to ethno-archaeological studies. She contributes essays and talks to notable platforms like The Conversation, Women’s Web, and Feminism in India. She engages in translating historical texts, directing plays and organizing cultural events. Among her accolades are the Elamkulam Kunjan Pillai Young Historian Prize, and the Erasmus Mundus Visiting Scholarship at Leiden University, Netherlands.

b: Dr. P V Unnikrishnan is a distinguished professional with over 37 years of experience spanning academia, research, government, and consulting. Specialising in EC Engineering and e-Gov, he has spearheaded critical…
f: Dr. P V Unnikrishnan is a distinguished professional with over 37 years of experience spanning academia, research, government, and consulting. Specialising in EC Engineering and e-Gov, he has spearheaded critical projects in decentralized planning, administrative reforms, service delivery and knowledge management. He has gained national and international recognition for his work in e-governance for local self-government institutions. He leads Kerala’s transition to a Knowledge Economy and has received numerous accolades.
s: From Recruit Train Deploy to Knowledge Transformation

b: Dr. Raheemudheen P.K. is a licensed Clinical Psychologist working under the Department of Health Services, Government of Kerala, currently posted at the Government Mental Health Centre, Kozhikode. He has more than 15…
f: Dr. Raheemudheen P.K. is a licensed Clinical Psychologist working under the Department of Health Services, Government of Kerala, currently posted at the Government Mental Health Centre, Kozhikode. He has more than 15 years of experience in mental health and disability rehabilitation. He previously served as the Joint Director of the CDMRP project and as Co-Chair of the UNESCO Chair on Community-Based Disability Management and Rehabilitation Studies. His areas of specialization include student mental health, cyber psychology, and disability management. He is one of the pioneers of the Behaviour Vaccine model, an innovative strategy to promote student well-being. He has presented over 12 research papers at national and international conferences, conducted more than 200 workshops, and received four Best Scientific Paper Awards. He has also co - edited 4 books and has been subject expert to various government bodies including the Education Department, Kerala Police, and SCERT.

b: Dr Rejeesh G R is a healthcare and medical technology professional with over 25 years of leadership experience spanning medical devices, blood transfusion systems, life sciences, and healthcare innovation ecosystems,…
f: Dr Rejeesh G R is a healthcare and medical technology professional with over 25 years of leadership experience spanning medical devices, blood transfusion systems, life sciences, and healthcare innovation ecosystems, across both Indian and global markets. He currently serves as General Manager (Marketing) at the Kerala Medical Technology Consortium (KMTC), a flagship initiative of the Government of Kerala, envisioned to position the state as the leading medical devices hub of the country by 2032. At the intersection of policy, practice, and purpose, his work reflects a strong belief that small states can lead big ideas—by aligning institutional capability, ethical governance, and innovation to create scalable impact. His interests also include community development, long-distance running for social causes, and mentoring young professionals transitioning into leadership roles.
s: Small State, Big Ideas: Kerala’s Blueprint for Mission-Driven Innovation

b: Dr. Santhosh Kumar S. S. is the Director of the United Nations Emergency Medical Team in Gaza and a Professor of Orthopaedics and Emergency Medicine at Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram. A surgeon,…
f: Dr. Santhosh Kumar S. S. is the Director of the United Nations Emergency Medical Team in Gaza and a Professor of Orthopaedics and Emergency Medicine at Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram. A surgeon, emergency director, and emergency medicine physician, he is an international trainer with experience across more than 40 countries, working in war zones, internal conflicts, and natural disasters. He is the author of the book Guns and Syringes and has published seven indexed articles in scientific journals. He is a recipient of the Kerala State Best Doctor Award and the Kairali Best Doctor Award.

f: Dr. Amjad Wafa is an Indian educationist, author, and influencer who is known for his innovative approach to holistic learning. He is the founder and director of Caliph Life School in Calicut which is recognized as India's first "Life School". In early 2026, he served as the Chief Curator for the Kerala Startup Fest (KSF '26). He is also a TEDx speaker and social media influencer. He has authored several books including The Forgotten Scientists Who Changed the World , The Unplugged Mind and Practical Islam , among others.

b: Dr Arathi P. M. is an interdisciplinary scholar whose academic interests lie at the intersection of law, gender, and public health. She currently teaches at the School of Indian Legal Thought and the School of Gender…
f: Dr Arathi P. M. is an interdisciplinary scholar whose academic interests lie at the intersection of law, gender, and public health. She currently teaches at the School of Indian Legal Thought and the School of Gender Studies at Mahatma Gandhi University. Her research engages critically with reproductive rights including abortion rights, new reproductive technologies, and surrogacy by examining the limits of law from an ethico-political perspective. Her highly acclaimed works include the novels The Thousand Faces of Night which won the Commonwealth Writers Prize for Best First Book in 1993, The Ghosts of Vasu Master , When Dreams Travel , Fugitive Histories and I Have Become the Tide , the short story collection The Art of Dying and the essay collection Almost Home: Cities and Other Places . f: Gokul S Pillai is an acclaimed Indian advertising filmmaker and founder of Storytellers Union, a creative studio renowned for fusing robust advertising expertise with cutting-edge technologies. His portfolio encompasses high-concept brand films, original intellectual property, and long-form content, increasingly incorporating AI-driven filmmaking techniques. He has collaborated with prominent brands such as Tata Tea, Britannia, Acko, Jio Hotstar, Airtel, AMD, Wonderla, and others, crafting campaigns that merge commercial precision with compelling narratives. He earned widespread recognition for "Dinomukku," a pioneering Malayalam mockumentary produced entirely with generative AI, which went viral nationwide and sparked discussions in creative and tech communities about agile, culturally resonant storytelling. Through Storytellers Union, he advances AI as a core creative asset at the nexus of culture, technology, and global narratives, with accolades including Good Ads Matter, Maddys, and Pepper Awards.

b: Guillermo Rodríguez is a multidisciplinary scholar, author, translator, cultural manager, and producer. He has published work in India, Spain, France, Poland, the U.K., and Germany. He is the Founding Director of Casa…
f: Guillermo Rodríguez is a multidisciplinary scholar, author, translator, cultural manager, and producer. He has published work in India, Spain, France, Poland, the U.K., and Germany. He is the Founding Director of Casa de la India in Valladolid, the pioneering Indian cultural centre in Spain, created in 2003 by the University of Valladolid, the City Council of Valladolid, and the Republic of India. Following a seven-year period of study and research in India during the 1990s, he returned to the University of Valladolid, where he served as Indian Studies Coordinator at the Centre for Asian Studies from 2000 to 2003. In 2012, he was awarded the Friendship Award by the Minister of External Affairs, Government of India, in recognition of his contribution to Indo-Spanish cultural relations. In 2016, he published When Mirrors Are Windows: A View of A.K. Ramanujan’s Poetics , a landmark book on the Indian poet-scholar. He is also the co-editor of Journeys: A Poet’s Diary and Soma: Poems by A.K. Ramanujan.

f: Hadija Haruna - Oelker is a German author , journalist and anchor . She writes and speaks about migration , race , racism , discrimination and the intersection of human identities . In 2025 , she co - authored Alles auf Anfang - Auf der Suche nach einer neuen Erinnerungskultur, Back to the Beginning – In Search of a New Culture of Remembrance with author Max Czollek .. Together they are hosts of the podcast Trauer & Turnschuh [ mourning & sneaker ] .

f: Harish Vasudevan is an Advocate practising before the High Court of Kerala & the National Green Tribunal, with over 13 years of specialised experience in environmental related and public interest litigation. He has been appointed as Amicus Curiae by the High Court of Kerala in several landmark environmental PILs. His work has led to significant judicial interventions in matters relating to illegal mining, wetland and mangrove conservation, Western Ghats protection, and enforcement of the EIA regime. He has successfully represented petitioners in cases resulting in closure of illegal mining and strengthening of environmental governance in India. He is a recipient of national and international recognitions, including fellowships from UC Berkeley and the U.S. State Department. He holds a BA(L), LL.B. from the University of Calicut.

f: Haritha Savithri is a writer, freelance journalist, human rights activist, and translator. She has published extensively in Malayalam journals and online portals, with a focus on Middle East politics and human rights violations. Her Malayalam translations include Iskender Pala’s Tulip of Istanbul , Elizabeth Louden’s A Stranger in Baghdad , Samar Yazbek’s The Crossing , and Ahmet Ümit’s The Cry of a Swallow . Her travelogue Murivettavarute Pathakal won the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Best Travelogue (2022). Her novel Zin received the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Best Novel (2023), the Kerala State Library Council’s Kadammanitta Award, and the Udya Sahitya Puraskaram (2023). She lives in Spain.

b: Helen Molesworth is a world-renowned jewellery historian and gemmologist with a 25-year career spanning the global gem and jewellery industry, from auction houses to academic posts. Her passion for gems has taken her…
f: Helen Molesworth is a world-renowned jewellery historian and gemmologist with a 25-year career spanning the global gem and jewellery industry, from auction houses to academic posts. Her passion for gems has taken her around the world, from the ruby mines of Burma and the emerald shafts of Colombia to the sapphire beds of Sri Lanka, as well as salerooms and collections from Paris to New York. For a decade, she served as a jewellery specialist at Sotheby’s and Christie’s in London and Geneva, where she managed major sales, including the private jewellery collection of HRH The Princess Margaret in 2006. She later held positions as Professeur d’Histoire du Bijoux at the Geneva University of Art and Design and as Managing Director of a gemmological academy operating across Switzerland and Asia. She is currently Senior Curator of Jewellery at the Victoria and Albert Museum, London, and Lead Curator of its blockbuster exhibition, Cartier . Her book, Precious: The History and Mystery of Gems Across Time , was released in 2024.
s: The History and Mystery of Gems across Times

f: Hrishikesh Bhaskaran serves as the VP of Engineering at Entri, a Kochi-based ed-tech startup, where he leads a team of developers to drive innovation in the education sector. With over 6.5 years in this role, he excels in strategy, software engineering, and product management, delivering solutions that improve learning outcomes and accessibility. A dedicated technology enthusiast, privacy advocate, Pythonista, and free software proponent, Hrishikesh has made significant contributions to language computing through Swathanthra Malayalam Computing, collaborating with organizations like Mozilla, Wikimedia, KITE, SCERT, and ICFOSS to advance open source technologies and digital literacy. He contributes to the privacy-focused PeARS Project for a decentralized peer-to-peer search engine, shares insights via college sessions and TV discussions on tech advancements, co-wrote the screenplay for the 2023 Malayalam film ‘Neelavelicham,’ and was a key architect of the ICU youth socio-cultural movement.

f: Ignacio García is a Mexican-American author and educator with extensive experience in theatre and performing arts. He is the programmer for Dramafest, a contemporary theatre festival in Mexico and has received a number of prestigious awards, including the Best Director Award from the Spanish Association of Stage Directors. He has directed theatrical productions and staged classic Hispanic texts in dozens of countries, developed workshops and masterclasses, and staged over 60 works from the universal repertoire across Europe and the Americas. He has also directed international dance productions, especially flamenco, and composed over 30 film scores with renowned directors.

b: Ikroop Sandhu is a graphic novelist and design educator . Her artistic practice centers on drawing and animation , exploring the feminine capacity for knowledge gathering, storytelling, and reflection. Her work is…
f: Ikroop Sandhu is a graphic novelist and design educator . Her artistic practice centers on drawing and animation , exploring the feminine capacity for knowledge gathering, storytelling, and reflection. Her work is deeply influenced by the feminist principle that " the personal is political " . She has collaborated on video art projects with prominent artists such as Raqs Media Collective, Sarnath Bannerjee and Mochu. Her illustrations have been showcased in The Print and Platform magazine and her work has been exhibited at IIT Gandhinagar . In 2022 , her debut graphic novel , Inquilab Zindabad , which chronicles the life of Punjabi revolutionary Bhagat Singh , was released by Yoda Press and Simon & Schuster. For the past two years, she has been dedicated to teaching storytelling , illustration , and animation , as well as developing curriculum at the Indian Institute of Art and Design (IIAD) in Delhi .
s: Germany’s Comics go Bold: Creative, Colorful, Experimental

b: Inga Marie Ramcke is a science educator based in Hamburg, Germany. She is a member of the children’s book writer network Elbautoren and focuses on non-fiction. Her books are published by German, Danish, and Russian…
f: Inga Marie Ramcke is a science educator based in Hamburg, Germany. She is a member of the children’s book writer network Elbautoren and focuses on non-fiction. Her books are published by German, Danish, and Russian publishing houses. Through the science communication project Plötzlich Wissen! (“Sudden Knowledge!”), she also works with adult audiences. Across both areas, she uses puppeteering to engage audiences of all ages with sustainable development topics. Her books cover space science, biology, and physics, while her adult work focuses on seas and oceans, combining playfulness, interaction, humour, and accessibility. Her approach encourages curiosity, dialogue, creativity, empathy, understanding, and scientific engagement.
s: ONCE UPON A DRAGONFLY AND OTHER STORIES OF ANIMAL MIGRATION

f: Ipsita Chakravarty is a journalist who has written and reported extensively on armed conflicts and identity politics in Kashmir and the states of North East India. In 2017, she won the RedInk Award for Reporting on Human Rights.In 2014, she won the Ramnath Goenka She has spent a decade and a half in newsrooms, including The Times of India, The Telegraph, The Indian Express and Scroll. With over 58,000 followers on Instagram (where he shares educational content on the environment and wildlife), he has gathered a strong and diverse audience across the country. His work has been featured on CNN-News18, Scroll, Mongabay, Times of India, Deccan Herald, The Better India , and more. He graduated Summa Cum Laude from Ashoka University, where he studied Environmental Studies, Entrepreneurship, and Sociology.

b: Ishita Shah is trained as an interior designer and an architectural historian. Over the last decade, she has been developing a community-based curatorial practice that focuses on cultural preservation and creative…
f: Ishita Shah is trained as an interior designer and an architectural historian. Over the last decade, she has been developing a community-based curatorial practice that focuses on cultural preservation and creative collaborations among individuals, families, and organisations, with the intention of deepening the culture of archiving in India and across South Asia. Two of her critical research and curatorial projects – Constructing Personal Archives, an incubation program for aspiring archivists, and the Women of Vaastukala Archive, a digital repository of oral histories of women practitioners – are situated under the aegis of a self-founded collective, Curating for Culture. Currently, she is a consulting archivist and/or curator with the Pattani Archives (Bhavnagar), Glenmorgan Estate (Ooty), and Shreyas Foundation (Ahmedabad). She has worked with several national and international organisations, teaches across various programs and cities, and has been awarded several acclaimed fellowships.

b: Jamling Tenzing Norgay , often called the “Son of the Everest Pioneer,” has forged his own path beyond a celebrated legacy. Renowned for his mountaineering expertise, he is a highly sought-after guide, leading both…
f: Jamling Tenzing Norgay , often called the “Son of the Everest Pioneer,” has forged his own path beyond a celebrated legacy. Renowned for his mountaineering expertise, he is a highly sought-after guide, leading both novices and seasoned climbers through some of the world’s most challenging terrain, carrying forward an ancient family profession into the modern era. He was selected as Climbing Leader of the international team that created the acclaimed IMAX documentary Everest . He has also made his mark in literature with Touching My Father’s Soul , an international bestseller that offers a poignant reflection on his relationship with his father and his own 1996 Everest ascent. Beyond physical achievements, he has been instrumental in bringing much-needed social services to remote Himalayan villages, with philanthropic contributions held in equal esteem to his mountaineering accomplishments.

This insight inspired him to co-found Elance, to drive innovation and excellence in finance education. f: Joel Joseph is a Malayali content creator whose character-driven comedy reflects the rhythm of Kerala’s everyday life. He has built a significant following by creating relatable reels that satirize everyday life in Indian, particularly Malayali households and his content often revolves around observational humour and character-based sketches. Through humour rooted in language, family dynamics, and cultural nuance, he creates narratives that feel both personal and widely relatable. His work bridges tradition and modern digital expression — using comedy not just to entertain, but to capture how Malayalees think, speak, and feel.

f: Jonas Lüscher is a novelist and essayist. After training as a primary school teacher in Bern, he worked in the film industry in Munich and studied philosophy at the Munich School of Philosophy, ETH Zurich, and Stanford University. His publications include the novella Spring of the Barbarians (2013), the novel Kraft (2017), the poetics lecture Fleeing into Storytelling (2020), and the novel Enchanted Determinism (2025). In addition to his literary work, he publishes political essays in German and international newspapers. His books have been published in more than twenty languages and have received numerous awards, including the Swiss Book Prize, the Franz Hessel Prize, the Max Frisch Prize, and the Wilhelm Raabe Prize.
s: The Quiet and the Political in Contemporary European Writing
Elected Dictators: When Democracy Becomes the Cover

b: Joseph K Jose, known popularly as Joseph Annamkutty Jose, is a popular author, influencer and radio personality. Known for his engaging talks, he has also conducted more than 150 talk shows around the world. In 2022, he…
f: Joseph K Jose, known popularly as Joseph Annamkutty Jose, is a popular author, influencer and radio personality. Known for his engaging talks, he has also conducted more than 150 talk shows around the world. In 2022, he was chosen as one of the Cultural Brand Ambassadors of India by the Ministry of Culture. He is also the only person from India who got selected to attend the International Visitor Leadership Program (IVLP) by the US state Government. He was also selected as the Best Radio Jockey (RJ) at the 2021 Creative Radio Awards. He currently hosts Stories with Joseph Annamkutty Jose in Radio Mirchi. Buried Thoughts , which has sold over 60 thousand copies and became a bestseller, Daivathinte Chaaranmar , which has sold over 1.6 lakh copies across the world and been selected as the Book of the Year by Amazon India and Sneham Kamam Branthu are a few of his best-selling works.

b: Joshil is a noted Malayalam writer. His debut work of fiction, Kadirakkam , explores the co-evolution of humankind and forests, set in the evocative landscape of a forest village in Wayanad. His second major work, the…
f: Joshil is a noted Malayalam writer. His debut work of fiction, Kadirakkam , explores the co-evolution of humankind and forests, set in the evocative landscape of a forest village in Wayanad. His second major work, the trilogy novel Aaru, Puzha, Nadhi… , is set against Kerala’s conservation movements and the political and social debates surrounding the construction of large dams. In addition to fiction, he regularly contributes articles to newspapers, periodicals, and online platforms, focusing on nature conservation and environmental law. He holds a postgraduate degree in Zoology and currently serves as Assistant Conservator of Forests at the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary. A trained Range Forest Officer from the Central Academy of State Forest Officers, Coimbatore, he has been associated with the Kerala Forest and Wildlife Department since 2006.

b: Joy Mathew is an Indian actor, playwright, director and political activist. He has written more than 20 plays in Malayalam including Athirthikkal , Sankadal and Poonaranga . Joy Mathew is best known for playing the lead…
f: Joy Mathew is an Indian actor, playwright, director and political activist. He has written more than 20 plays in Malayalam including Athirthikkal , Sankadal and Poonaranga . Joy Mathew is best known for playing the lead role in John Abraham's 1986 film Amma Ariyan which was voted one of the Top 10 Indian films by British Film Institute. Shutter, his first film, had its Indian premiere at the 17th International Film Festival of Kerala and international premiere at the 9th Dubai International Film Festival. It won the Silver Crow Pheasant Award for Best Feature Film (Audience Prize) at the 17th International Film Festival of Kerala. He was honoured by Kerala Sahitya Academy and Sangeeta Nataka Academy for two of his plays in 1995 and 1996. He won the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for the play Madhya Dharanazh i.

She has written the story and screenplay for the anthology film Padachonte Kathaka l and for short films such as Sindhoora KL Oru Mediterranean Yathra and Hridhi . She is also a lyricist. Some of her notable works include Charuhaasini, Theendari, Symphony and 51 Akshara Kavithakal.

b: K.C. Venugopal is a veteran Indian legislator who currently serves as a Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) for Alappuzha, Kerala, and holds the powerful position of AICC General Secretary (Organisation). With a political…
f: K.C. Venugopal is a veteran Indian legislator who currently serves as a Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) for Alappuzha, Kerala, and holds the powerful position of AICC General Secretary (Organisation). With a political career spanning over three decades, Venugopal has held significant roles in both state and national governance. He previously served as the Union Minister of State for Civil Aviation and Power (2011–2014) and represented Rajasthan in the Rajya Sabha (2020–2024). Currently, he serves as the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), one of the Indian Parliament's most critical oversight bodies. Known for his organisational acumen and deep-rooted experience in parliamentary affairs, Venugopal rose through the ranks from student leadership to become a trusted advisor within the Congress high command. He is a frequent voice on national policy, human rights, and constitutional governance.

b: K Jayakumar is an acclaimed poet, translator and lyricist. He has authored 47 books including 14 anthologies of poems in Malayalam and English. His important translations into Malayalam include Gitanjali of Tagore, The…
f: K Jayakumar is an acclaimed poet, translator and lyricist. He has authored 47 books including 14 anthologies of poems in Malayalam and English. His important translations into Malayalam include Gitanjali of Tagore, The Prophet of Kahlil Gibran and the poetry of Rumi. He has also translated the works of the famous author ONV Kurup’s poetry into English. He has retired from the Indian Administrative Service as the Chief Secretary of Kerala and also has served as the founding Vice Chancellor of Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University. He is the recipient of several awards that include the Kerala Sahitya Academy for overall contribution, the Kerala Sangeeta Nataka Academy for lyrics and the Central Sahitya Akademi award for poetry. Sancharathinte Sangeetham , Lalithajeevitham, Ode To Orpheus , 100 Kabir Kavithakal are some of his acclaimed works among others.

Jayachandran, often recording tracks that helped launch popular songs like "Mayangippoyi" and "Kandu Kandu".

His research engages with issues of land, labour and unfreedom in Pre-Modern Kerala, caste and social Hierarchy. A former visiting fellow at CHS JNU , he has published research articles in national and international journals. His notable works include Caste Class and Hindutva and Explorations in South Indian History (edited volume)and studies on Dalit movements and social history.

She has authored and published books including Ormakurippukal and Ormayile Theenalangal. She has also participated in international events like the UN Conference on CEDAW and World Court of Women against War, for Peace. She has been honoured with numerous accolades including the Jana Samskruti Award, Lakshmi Award by Sahrudaya Vedi and the Yuga Deepam Sam Award.

b: K. Satish Nambudiripad is the Director General of the North-East Zone of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B), Government of India. He heads the offices of the Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Central…
f: K. Satish Nambudiripad is the Director General of the North-East Zone of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B), Government of India. He heads the offices of the Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) for the entire North Eastern region. In this capacity, he supervises and oversees media outreach and communication strategies of the Government of India in the Eight North-Eastern States. He was, till recently, Head of Electronic Media Monitoring Centre (EMMC) and New Media Wing (NMW), two of the futuristic media organisations under the Ministry of I&B, in Delhi, as also ADG (Admn & Training), Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). Nambudiripad has also held, during his 33-year long career, positions such as Private Secretary to Union Minister for Food & Public Distribution and Consumer Affairs, Director (Secondary Education) and Registrar of Copyrights India in the Union Ministry of Human Resources Development, Deputy Press Secretary to the President of India, late Dr. K.R. Narayanan and Information Officer to National Human Rights Commission (NHRC). As the first Chief Executive Officer of the NORKA Department (Non-Resident Keralites’ Affairs), he is credited with setting up NORKA-ROOTs, the implementing agency of the Department. Deeply interested in topics related to education, employment, migration and media, he has been contributing articles on developmental and social issues to newspapers and journals and delivering lectures at various fora. He is also interested in all forms of artistic and cultural expression, music as well as reading.

b: K.E.N Kunjahammed is a left-wing intellectual, writer and orator. He is one of the secretaries of the Progressive Arts and Literature Society. E. N. Kunjahammed is also a member of the Executive Committee of the Kerala…
f: K.E.N Kunjahammed is a left-wing intellectual, writer and orator. He is one of the secretaries of the Progressive Arts and Literature Society. E. N. Kunjahammed is also a member of the Executive Committee of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi. Writing in journals and newspapers upholding the left's stand, K. E. N. has authored about thirty books. He is a strong advocate of Marxist thought and Left politics in Kerala.

b: K. N. Ajoy Kumar is a social and educational professional whose work engages the public in critical discussions on education, ecology, science, and the broader dimensions of politics. A former Associate Professor at…
f: K. N. Ajoy Kumar is a social and educational professional whose work engages the public in critical discussions on education, ecology, science, and the broader dimensions of politics. A former Associate Professor at Nirmalagiri College, he currently serves as Faculty and Course Director of Plant Science at Kannur University, and functions as a resource person specializing in education, ecology, and the philosophy and ethics of science. His work follows an interdisciplinary approach, bridging education, science, and ethics. He has published scholarly articles in edited volumes by international publishers such as Springer Nature and Elsevier, as well as in reputed international scientific journals. His writings have also appeared in edited books and leading Malayalam magazines, including Mathrubhumi and Malayalam Weekly, with contributions spanning science, education, and the wider spheres of politics.

b: Kai Tuchmann graduated in directing from Hochschule für Schauspielkunst Ernst Busch in Berlin and works as a dramaturg, director, and academic. His documentary theatre works have explored the afterlife of the Cultural…
f: Kai Tuchmann graduated in directing from Hochschule für Schauspielkunst Ernst Busch in Berlin and works as a dramaturg, director, and academic. His documentary theatre works have explored the afterlife of the Cultural Revolution in contemporary China, the impact of urbanisation on migrant workers in Europe and Asia, and the role of the body in the face of digital technologies. His works have been showcased at i-Dance Hong Kong, Zürcher Theater Spektakel, Festival d’Automne à Paris, and documenta Institut, among others. Tuchmann co-developed the first BA dramaturgy curriculum in Asia at the Central Academy of Drama in Beijing, where he was a visiting professor. He has researched the history of dramaturgy as a Fulbright Scholar at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York, and worked as a curator for the Ludics Seminar at Harvard University.
s: Theatre In The Age Of Legal And Political Precarity

b: Kaithapram Damodharan Namboothiri , popularly known as Kaithapram, is a legendary Indian lyricist, music director, poet, and singer primarily active in Malayalam cinema. In 2021, he was awarded the Padma Shri, India’s…
f: Kaithapram Damodharan Namboothiri , popularly known as Kaithapram, is a legendary Indian lyricist, music director, poet, and singer primarily active in Malayalam cinema. In 2021, he was awarded the Padma Shri, India’s fourth-highest civilian honor, for his profound contributions to the arts. He started composing music in 1997 with Kottapurathe Koottukudumbam and is known for his work in films like Deshadanam . His work also includes screenwriting, acting, and directing. A pioneer in music therapy in India, Kaithapram established the Swathi Thirunal Kalakendram Trust and the Music Therapy Foundation to use music for healing. He has received multiple Kerala State Film Awardsfor Best Lyricist, including for Paithrukam (1993) and Azhakiya Ravanan (1996), and for Best Music Director for Deshadanam (1996).

b: Kalpetta Narayanan is a poet and critic. His major poetry anthologies include Samayaprabhu , Ethilayum Madhurikkunna Kadukalil , and Orkkapurangal . His novels are Ithramathram and Evidamividam . He has also published…
f: Kalpetta Narayanan is a poet and critic. His major poetry anthologies include Samayaprabhu , Ethilayum Madhurikkunna Kadukalil , and Orkkapurangal . His novels are Ithramathram and Evidamividam . He has also published numerous studies, works of criticism, and general essays; Ente Basheer is a collection of essays on the literary world of Vaikom Muhammed Basheer. In addition, he writes columns for newspapers and magazines. He has received numerous awards, including the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Awards for Poetry and Literary Criticism in 2017.

b: Kamal Varadoor is an Indian journalist from Kerala, best known for his work in Malayalam media and sports journalism. He is the Editor-in-Chief at Chandrika daily newspaper, a Malayalam publication. He has covered…
f: Kamal Varadoor is an Indian journalist from Kerala, best known for his work in Malayalam media and sports journalism. He is the Editor-in-Chief at Chandrika daily newspaper, a Malayalam publication. He has covered numerous major sports events, including Asian Games, FIFA World Cups, Olympics, and more, gaining recognition in sports reporting. He has served in leadership roles such as President of the Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ)and Calicut Press Club President, Secretary ,Sports faculty at Institute of Journalism in Calicut Press Club. He has has received several awards for his contributions to journalism, especially sports reporting, including Kerala State Sports Award for Best Sports Reporter. He has also authored a book titled Bonjour Paris , a travelogue published in Malayalam.

b: Kamalakar Bhat is an award-winning Kannada poet, teaching at Ahmednagar College, Maharashtra. He is a bilingual writer and translator. He has published four collections of poems, six collections of translated verse, and…
f: Kamalakar Bhat is an award-winning Kannada poet, teaching at Ahmednagar College, Maharashtra. He is a bilingual writer and translator. He has published four collections of poems, six collections of translated verse, and has edited four books. He writes in both academic and popular media on books, poetry, and translations. His most recent work is a translation of the essays of Kirtinath Kurtkoti, titled Courtesy of Criticism , published by Penguin Random House India. He is the recipient of the PUTINA Award, the BH Shridhar Award, and the Mozhi Prize for translation.
s: Translation and the Making of Archives

b: Kanwal Rekhi was the first Indo-American founder and CEO to take a venture-backed company public on NASDAQ. He founded and built The IndUS Entrepreneurs (TiE) into the world’s largest global network of Indian…
f: Kanwal Rekhi was the first Indo-American founder and CEO to take a venture-backed company public on NASDAQ. He founded and built The IndUS Entrepreneurs (TiE) into the world’s largest global network of Indian entrepreneurs and co-founded Inventus Capital Partners, where he continues to devote his time, energy, and leadership to building a venture franchise that serves as a catalyst for India’s technology revolution. He came to the United States from India for graduate studies, rose through engineering leadership roles across multiple technology companies, and went on to co-found Excelan in Silicon Valley. Excelan commercialized Ethernet and TCP/IP standards that later became the foundation of the modern internet. His book The Groundbreaker: Entrepreneurship, the American Dream, and the Rise of Modern India was published recently.
s: Building with Purpose: Leadership, Legacy, and the Entrepreneurial Spirit

b: Karishma Mehrotra is an Indian-American journalist who is currently the South Asia correspondent for the Washington Post. A Fulbright fellow, she has worked for Radiolab, the Wall Street Journal, CNN, the Indian…
f: Karishma Mehrotra is an Indian-American journalist who is currently the South Asia correspondent for the Washington Post. A Fulbright fellow, she has worked for Radiolab, the Wall Street Journal, CNN, the Indian Express, Scroll.in, and Bloomberg Businessweek . She was part of a team that was nominated for the Pulitzer. She has also won grants and awards from RedInk, The Society of Publishers in Asia, the South Asian Journalism Association, and the Earth Journalism Network.
s: Diplomacy in the Age of AI

b: Kavitha Balakrishnan is an accomplished artist, author, and art history researcher. Her first book, Artek Anubhavangal (Vishwadarshan Books, 2003), is a travelogue recounting her experiences in the Soviet Union. She has…
f: Kavitha Balakrishnan is an accomplished artist, author, and art history researcher. Her first book, Artek Anubhavangal (Vishwadarshan Books, 2003), is a travelogue recounting her experiences in the Soviet Union. She has also published several acclaimed works, including Ankavalulla Pakshi (Rainbow Books, 2004), Njan Jassund (DC Books, 2007), and Kavithayute Kavitakal (Tamara Books, 2017). Together, these works mark Kerala’s historical engagement with national and international contemporary art movements. She has made foundational contributions to art history writing through essays and articles in both English and Malayalam. Her work has earned her numerous prestigious honors, including the Kerala Lalitha Kala Sahitya Akademi Award and the G. N. Pillai Endowment Award. She is currently the Head of the Department of Art History at the Government College of Fine Arts, Thrissur.
s: Kerala Modern: Mapping Art and Culture

f: Khyrunnisa A. is an award-winning writer of children’s fiction. She created the popular comic character Butterfingers for Tinkle and authored the much-loved Butterfingers series for older children, published by Penguin Random House (Puffin). Her work Smash It, Butterfingers! was shortlisted for the Sahitya Akademi's Bal Sahitya Puraskar in 2024.Some of her other notable works include The Lizard of Oz and Other Stories , The Crocodile Who Ate Butter Chicken for Breakfast and Other Stories , and Baby and Dubdub . She has also written two books for adults: Tongue in Cheek: The Funny Side of Life and Chuckle Merry Spin: Us in the U.S. In 2024, she released a picture book, Ka Kha Ga , illustrated by Monami Roy and published by DC Books.

f: Krupa Ge is a Chennai-based author whose written works include Burns Boy (2025) and What We Know About Her (2021) . Her nonfiction work, Rivers Remember (2019), examines the impact of the devastating 2015 Chennai floods, weaving together personal, social and environmental narratives. In 2024, Zubaan published Ramachandran Usha’s Tamil novella Karai Thedum Odangal , as Unmoored , in Krupa’s translation. She collaborated with musician and Sangita Kalanidhi awardee, Sanjay Subrahmanyan on his memoir, On That Note (2024). Her work, spanning reportage and cultural commentary, has appeared in Indian and international publications for 17 years.
s: Translation and the Making of Archives

Searching for a new Memory Culture) together with Hadja Haruna-Oelker, with whom he has hosted the podcast Trauer und Turnschuh since 2023.

b: Morangam Khaling (known as Mo Naga) is an ethnic Uipo Naga tattoo artist. Originally from the north-eastern Indian state of Manipur, he trained as a fashion designer at the National Institute of Fashion Technology in…
f: Morangam Khaling (known as Mo Naga) is an ethnic Uipo Naga tattoo artist. Originally from the north-eastern Indian state of Manipur, he trained as a fashion designer at the National Institute of Fashion Technology in Hyderabad, where he started tattooing almost ten years ago. After tattooing professionally in New Delhi for several years, he left the capital in 2013 to open the first tattoo studio and tattoo school in Guwahati, the gateway city to the Naga homeland. His school is dedicated to promoting Naga tattoo art and culture through contemporary renditions of traditional patterns and responsible tattooing. Mo Naga avoids foreign tattoo designs as believes that the ones that Naga youth see are completely foreign to their culture. He emphasises on developing tattoo designs inspired by local indigenous Naga art and heritage, making the art of tattooing more meaningful and acceptable.
s: Indian Tattoos: Only Skin Deep? Tattooed in India, Rooted in Culture

He is the author of the books Bezoar Delinqxenz (Edith-Russ-Haus + Sternberg Press, 2023), and Nervous Fossils: Syndromes of the Synthetic Nether (Reliable Copy + KNMA, 2022). He is a recipient of fellowships from Edith-Russ-Haus für Medienkunst (2020-22), Ashkal Alwan (2015-16), India Foundation for the Arts (2012-15) and The Sarai Programme (2012). Exhibitions include at RMIT Melbourne (2024), 9th Asian Art Biennial (2024), HKW (2024), Whitechapel Gallery (2023), 9th Asia-Pacific Triennial (2018), 4th Kochi-Muziris Biennale (2018), 13th Sharjah Biennial (2017) and transmediale:BWPWAP (2013), with a solo show at Edith-Russ-Haus für Medienkunst (2022).

f: Naaji Noushi is an inspiring solo overland traveller from Kerala and a mother of five who has redefined what is possible for women on the road. Challenging social norms and logistical barriers, she travels solo across countries by road, using an Indian-made Mahindra Thar as her trusted companion. Her journey began in 2020 with a 5,000 km road trip across Kerala, followed by a 16,000 km drive covering the length and breadth of India in 2021. The same year, she explored ten islands of Lakshadweep and trekked to the Everest Base Camp in Nepal over five days. f: Necati Öziri is a prominent German writer and dramaturg. He studied philosophy, German studies, and contemporary German literature in Bochum, Istanbul, and Berlin. He was a scholarship recipient of the Heinrich Böll Foundation and taught formal logic at Ruhr University Bochum until he realized that logic does not describe the world particularly well. From 2014 to 2017, he worked as a dramaturg at Berlin’s Maxim Gorki Theatre, including two years as artistic director of Studio Я. After that, he headed the International Forum of Germany’s most renowned theatre festival, the Theatertreffen of the Berliner Festspiele. As a playwright, he writes for the Maxim Gorki Theatre, the National Theatre Mannheim—where he also served as playwright-in-residence—the Schauspielhaus Zürich, and many others. At the 45th Days of German-Language Literature (Ingeborg Bachmann Prize), he won both the Kelag Prize and the Audience Award. His novel Vatermal (Ullstein/Claassen, 2023) was shortlisted for the German Book Prize, awarded the Ruhr Literature Prize and the Hölderlin Förderpreis, and has already been staged by three theatres. He lives and works in Berlin.

Her notable works include Ennekkumulla Orma , Aa Raavu Pularaathirunnirenkil , and Kaalathinte Kaaloccha , among others. b: Shabnam Virmani is a prominent Indian documentary filmmaker, singer, and artist known for her extensive work exploring the 15th century mystic poet Kabir and other Bhakti-Sufi traditions. In the wake of the 2002…
f: Shabnam Virmani is a prominent Indian documentary filmmaker, singer, and artist known for her extensive work exploring the 15th century mystic poet Kabir and other Bhakti-Sufi traditions. In the wake of the 2002 communal riots in Gujarat, Virmani set out to explore the philosophy of Kabir and other mystics through a deep engagement with their oral folk traditions for over two decades. Her inspiration and joy in this poetry and its wisdom has taken the shape of several documentary films, a digital archive called Ajab Shahar, singing and performing herself, writing books, curating urban festivals and rural yatras and building a new schools program called Shabad Shaala. The culmination of her work on Kabir, named the Kabir Project, is housed at the Srishti Manipal Institute in Bangalore. Earlier she has worked on gender issues through journalism, video and radio work in the community. Her written works include I Saw Myself, One Palace A Thousand Doorways and Burn Down Your House.

He holds a Master’s degree in Strategic Marketing from the University of Wollongong, UAE, and has been instrumental in driving Kenza Steel’s growth through a strong commitment to innovation and excellence. Under his leadership, key strategies have been implemented to modernize production processes and strengthen marketing initiatives within a sustainable business framework. Recognizing the potential of the digital-first generation, he built a dynamic team that effectively leverages technology and social media to engage customers and accelerate business expansion. In 2017, he received the “Outstanding Young Entrepreneur” award from the Central Ministry, presented by Union Minister of State for Finance, Arjun Ram Meghwal. This recognition underscored his leadership and established him as a role model for young entrepreneurs.

f: Shahina K K is a senior journalist based in Kerala with over 28 years of experience across television, print, and digital media. She is the founder and Chief Editor of OBC Off Beat Concerns, a grassroots media literacy and fact checking organisation. Her works have earned major honours, including the CPJ International Press Freedom Award 2023, the Chameli Devi Jain Award, and the Kerala State Media Award, which she became the first woman journalist to receive in 2002–03. She is a postgraduate in English Literature and a law graduate with specialisation in in Human Rights Law from the National Law University. She currently resides in Kochi, Kerala.
s: What India Loses When South India is Undermined? Who gets to be Angry in South India?

f: Sham Salim is a certified architect and spatial designer , and the co-founder of the multi-award winning design practice @aslamsham_architects based in Calicut, India. s: Temporary, Yet Timeless: Meaning Memory, and the Pavillion

Ummer Award, each celebrating her artistic excellence and commitment to music.
