b: Sophie d’Aubreby is a writer born in Brussels and raised in the south of France. Her debut novel S'en aller (Inculte, 2021) followed the short story Déplier les jambes (Lamiroy, 2020), and her prose piece Je me loge…
f: Sophie d’Aubreby is a writer born in Brussels and raised in the south of France. s: Compassionate Spaces: A Right or a Privilege

f: Sunny Paikkada is a farmer and Gandhian frontline campaigner with roots in Melukavu village of Pala, Kottayam district, and currently residing in Konnakkadu, Kasaragod district, Kerala. b: Syed Rashad Imam Tanmoy , known simply as Tanmoy, is a Bangladeshi comic book artist and publisher whose work spans political satire, comics, and children’s literature. His practice ranges from autobiographical graphic…
f: Syed Rashad Imam Tanmoy , known simply as Tanmoy, is a Bangladeshi comic book artist and publisher whose work spans political satire, comics, and children’s literature. His practice ranges from autobiographical graphic novels to fantasy and science-fiction comics, as well as comics created for social change. Over the past decade, he has contributed to leading national newspapers, addressing themes of free speech, social justice, and human rights. In 2016, he founded Cartoon People, a creative community of young visual storytellers dedicated to nurturing Bangladesh’s local comics scene. Expanding this vision, he established Cartoon People Comics in 2022, an independent publishing house committed to taking Bangladeshi stories to global audiences. His work explores comics as a bridge between art, activism, and education. He collaborates with the international non-profit Artolution, using comics and murals to foster community dialogue in underprivileged areas, including Rohingya refugee camps. A World Press Institute Journalism Fellow (2015) and IVLP Edward R. Murrow Journalism Program Fellow (2014), Tanmoy has led several art-for-change initiatives, including Cartoons for Equality with UN Women and Girls Do Comics , encouraging young Bangladeshi women to express their voices through the medium. His work has been exhibited nationally and internationally and featured in leading publications.

f: 2011 — Metallica played in India for the first time. It was an experience of raw, unfiltered energy. Aditi and Akshay were there - and around the same time, they had just founded Purple Ink. That same energy would go on to shape the studio’s spirit — unapologetic, cultural, and personal. Over the years, the studio grew with Principals Nishita Bhatia and Arpita Pai, evolving into a practice that is homegrown at its core: built on craft and clarity, bold in approach, and deeply Indian in spirit. The studio’s work has been recognised globally — featured among The 220 Best Architectural Firms Worldwide (Architizer 2025) and awarded World Architecture Community Building of the Year 2025 for the TAPMI Center. It has also been a finalist at the World Architecture Festival (2024, 2025), Dezeen Awards 2025, and PLAN Awards, Italy (2023–25), and honoured by FORBES India 30under45, Perspective Hong Kong’s 40under40 Asia, and TRENDS Excellence Awards 2016 for Best Practice in India, among other recognitions. f: V. D. Satheesan is a distinguished Indian politician and the current Leader of the Opposition in the Kerala Legislative Assembly. A five-term Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) representing the Paravur constituency since 2001, he is a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress and the United Democratic Front (UDF). A lawyer by profession with a practice history at the High Court of Kerala, he is widely recognised for his articulate parliamentary interventions and legal expertise. He is also an active trade unionist, and the president or various worker's organisations across the Cochin industrial belt. Throughout his career, he has held several key positions, including Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee and Chief Whip of the Congress Legislature Party.

f: V.Selvakumar is an archaeologist specializing in Prehistory, Neolithic Culture, Iron Age Megaliths, Historical Archaeology and Maritime Archaeology of South India; Public Archaeology, Heritage Management and Indian Ocean interactions. He completed his studies from the University of Madras and University of Poona (Ph.D. Deccan College). He was a Visiting Researcher at the Centre for Maritime Archaeology, Southampton, UK, in 2004. He has worked at Centre for Heritage Studies, Tripunithura, Kerala, and Department of Epigraphy and Archaeology, Tamil University, Thanjavur. He was a Scholar-in-Residence at KCHR, Thiruvananthapuram (2023). Currently he is the Head of the Department of Maritime History and Marine Archaeology, and Coordinator, Centre for Indian Ocean Studies,Tamil University, Thanjavur. He has published several books and research papers.

f: V Sunil Kumar, an entrepreneur and pioneer of innovation in the real estate sector is also a notable author. He founded Asset Homes, one of Kerala’s leading real estate brands, in 2007. Some of his books include Khader, Myth and Realty, Bulit To Last, Susthira Nurmithikal And Co-Veedu days- 21 Days Lockdown Musings, which is published as an E-book as well, and his latest book, a collection of his social media videos, Reel Estate.

b: V. Abdurahiman is a prominent politician serving as the current Minister of Sports, Waqf and Haj pilgrimage, Railways, Posts and Telegraph in the Government of Kerala. He has a long political trajectory, evolving from a…
f: V. Abdurahiman is a prominent politician serving as the current Minister of Sports, Waqf and Haj pilgrimage, Railways, Posts and Telegraph in the Government of Kerala. He has a long political trajectory, evolving from a local student leader to a state minister. He entered politics through the Kerala Students Union (KSU) and later held key roles in the Youth Congress. He served for 15 years as a Councillor in the Tirur Municipality, where he also held the positions of Vice-Chairman and Standing Committee Chairman. He was a member of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) until 2014, when he left the Congress party to contest the Ponnani Lok Sabha seat as an LDF-backed independent. He was first elected to the Kerala Legislative Assembly from Tanur in 2016 and retained the seat in 2021.

b: V. Muzafer Ahamed is a celebrated travel writer known for his deep explorations of the Arab desert and storytelling that blends adventure, culture, and reflection. His acclaimed travelogue Marubhumiyude Atmakatha ( The…
f: V. Muzafer Ahamed is a celebrated travel writer known for his deep explorations of the Arab desert and storytelling that blends adventure, culture, and reflection. His acclaimed travelogue Marubhumiyude Atmakatha ( The Autobiography of the Desert ) won the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award in 2010 and was part of the Calicut University curriculum for five years. Its English translation, Camels in the Sky , was used as a textbook at Troy University, USA. Along with travel, his writings also explore diverse themes such as Indian spiritual traditions, marginalized voices, and cultural heritage.

f: ﻿ Vaishali Shroff is an engineer-turned, award-winning author, scriptwriter, and columnist based in Mumbai. With over 300 published stories—fiction and non-fiction—her work appears in books, textbooks, magazines, newspapers, and digital media across Indian and international publishing houses. Published by leading houses, she has spent the last fourteen years writing children’s books. Her pioneering paleontology title, The Adventures of Padma and a Blue Dinosaur , and her debut film script Rajasaur have won multiple awards at international film festivals. Her recent works include Ganesh Pyne’s Twilight Dreams , 10 Indian Scientists , and Submerged Worlds and Other Amazing Stories of India’s Mighty Rivers .
s: Writing the Unseen, Unheard, and Unexplored

f: Veerankutty is a distinguished poet, translator and social critic from Kerala. His work Mindaprani won the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Poetry and his poems have been featured in Poetry International Magazine and translated into several languages. Other notable works include Jalabhoopadam , Papillon , Manthrikan , Manveeru , and Thottu Thottu Nadakkumbol . He has received several numerous awards, including the Cherusseri Award. He was part of the Poets Translating Poets project conducted by Goethe Institute in collaboration with UNESCO. His poems are widely studied in schools and universities.

b: N. Venugopal, popularly known as Venu is a National Award–winning filmmaker and director who works predominantly in the Malayalam film industry. He has worked as a Director of Photography for nearly 100 feature films…
f: N. Venugopal, popularly known as Venu is a National Award–winning filmmaker and director who works predominantly in the Malayalam film industry. He has worked as a Director of Photography for nearly 100 feature films across various languages. He is the recipient of several prestigious honours, including the National Film Award for Best Cinematography (three times), the Indira Gandhi National Award for Best Debut Director (once), the Kerala State Film Award for Best Cinematography (three times), and the Kerala State Film Award for Best Debut Director (once). His other accolades include the CTA Technician of the Year (India) and the Best Cinematographer Award from the Asia Film Academy, London. He has directed three feature films and one short film in Malayalam. Some of his notable works as a DOP include Maati Manas , Amma Ariyan , But I Have Promises to Keep , Manichithra Thaazhu , Guna , Innale , Vadakkunokkiyanthram, Minsara kanavu and Dasharatham , spanning multiple film industries. He is also the author of a number of books, including Solo Stories , Nagnarum Narabhojikalum , and Chilar Chilappol .

f: Vinil Paul is an author, a passionate educator and researcher, committed to examining the intricate social and cultural transformations that have shaped Kerala’s history. His research spans a wide array of topics, including slavery, Protestant Christian missionary movements, Dalit Christian histories, colonial hunting practices, agricultural labourers and global history. His notable works include Adima Keralathinte Adrushya Charithram , Mrugaya: Keralathinte Nayattucharithram and Dalit Charithradamshanam . He is an Assistant Professor of History at Fatima Mata National College, Kollam.

f: Vinod Chellan is a researcher at Cochin University of Science and Technology, focusing on the Chelanayakkan , Kaatunayakkan community and their socio-economic conditions. He presented his research thesis on the Chelanayakkan community at the Arctic University of Norway. Currently, he continues to work closely with the community, actively engaging with their broader socio-cultural concerns and lived realities.

b: Vipin V. C . currently works with K-DISC’s “One Local Government One Idea (OLOI)” programme, supporting local self-governments in solving developmental issues through innovation by enabling multi-stakeholder…
f: Vipin V. C . currently works with K-DISC’s “One Local Government One Idea (OLOI)” programme, supporting local self-governments in solving developmental issues through innovation by enabling multi-stakeholder coordination, grassroots problem-solving, and local economic development. He is a PhD research scholar focusing on designing an innovation model for local self-governments. He has also served in Kerala’s community development ecosystem, including as a State Assistant Program Manager with Kudumbashree. b: Vivek Karunakaran has been a distinctive voice in Indian fashion, for over 18 years, seamlessly fusing rooted tradition with contemporary elegance. Voted among the 50 Best Dressed Men in India by GQ Magazine for four…
f: Vivek Karunakaran has been a distinctive voice in Indian fashion, for over 18 years, seamlessly fusing rooted tradition with contemporary elegance. Voted among the 50 Best Dressed Men in India by GQ Magazine for four consecutive years, he is not just a designer but an embodiment of style himself. Driven by a spirit of individuality and progressive thinking, he designs for spirited men and women who fearlessly represent what they believe in. His creations reinterpret Indian textiles like Kalamkari and Kanjeevaram, translating them into sharply modern, globally relevant forms. Renowned for his clean, minimal and structured aesthetic, he has been instrumental in putting Chennai on the fashion map. His collections, showcased at Lakmé Fashion Week, India Fashion Week and prestigious runways across the world, pay homage to Indian craft and heritage while pushing the boundaries of modern design.
s: South India, Seen Anew: Reframing Regional Aesthetics for a Global Eye

b: Y. Muhammed Anvar is an Assistant Conservator of Forests currently working at the Forest Headquarters, Thiruvananthapuram. He serves as the State Nodal Officer of Mission Sarpa , a pioneering initiative aimed at…
f: Y. Muhammed Anvar is an Assistant Conservator of Forests currently working at the Forest Headquarters, Thiruvananthapuram. He serves as the State Nodal Officer of Mission Sarpa , a pioneering initiative aimed at reducing casualties caused by snakebite. Under his stewardship over five years, the programme has significantly reduced fatalities and trained more than four thousand individuals in safe snake rescue and release. Deeply committed to wildlife awareness, he regularly delivers public lectures and writes articles, particularly on snakes and human–reptile coexistence. Trained originally as a Mechanical Engineer, his work in conservation communication is driven by passion, field experience, and unwavering dedication.
